_comment: Every field here is read from an official SRMIST document the learner
supplied, and the source is recorded so somebody can check it. Nothing
is inferred: a fact no source states is left empty.
The syllabus is the 2026 regulation. The papers the learner supplied are
from the earlier regulation and carry the old course code, so both codes
are recorded and the difference is shown rather than smoothed over.
The question bank is NOT here. Past papers and question banks are the
learner's own material and are not ours to redistribute, so the bank
lives in the app's data directory and is written by

courses.title: Programming for Problem Solving
courses.institution: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
courses.regulation: B.Tech / M.Tech (Integrated) Regulations 2026, Volume 2 - Syllabi for First Year Courses
courses.syllabus_source: Official SRMIST academic curriculum PDF supplied by the learner: 'Academic Curricula, Undergraduate/Integrated and Postgraduate Degree Programmes (Choice Based Flexible Credit System), Regulations 2026, Volume 2'. The course entry is on printed page 62 (PDF page 62).
courses.syllabus_version: Regulations 2026, approved by the 62nd Academic Council on 07/03/2026
courses.exam_pattern: Continuous assessment 50% (CA-1 written test 15%, CA-2 written test or examination 15%, CA-3 practice 20%) and a summative final examination 50% (theory 30%, practice 30%). The syllabus states the assessment split and the Bloom-level distribution; it does not state a question-paper pattern, so none is asserted here.

assessment.bloom_levels: Remember 30%, Understand 30%, Apply and Analyze 70/70/40/70%, Evaluate and Create 30%
assessment.cla_mapping: CLA-1 covers Units I to II, CLA-2 covers Units III to V, CLA-3 covers Units I to V

outcomes: CLO-1 Implement decision constructs to solve programming problems.
CLO-2 Apply functions and recursion to solve subproblems.
CLO-3 Use arrays, strings, and loops to solve problems.
CLO-4 Analyze and apply iterative-recursive logic efficiently.
CLO-5 Use structures and dynamic memory to manage heterogeneous and large input data.
rationale: CLR-1 Develop logical decision-making skills for programming.
CLR-2 Promote problem decomposition and modular program design.
CLR-3 Build foundational skills in data storage and iteration.
CLR-4 Strengthen problem-solving through nested loops and recursion.
CLR-5 Integrate structures, memory management, and file handling.
references: R. G. Dromey, How to Solve It by Computer, Pearson, 2020
Jeri R. Hanly and Elliot B. Koffman, Problem Solving and Program Design in C, Pearson, 2023
Behrouz A. Forouzan and Richard F. Gilberg, C: A Problem-Solving Approach, Cengage, 2023
Greg Perry and Dean Miller, C Programming Absolute Beginner's Guide, Pearson, 2023
H. S. Natarajan, The Art of Problem Solving with C, PHI Learning, 2021
Prof. Satyadev Nandakumar and Team (IIT Madras), NPTEL - Problem Solving Through Programming in C
S. Sridhar, S. S. Sridhar and V. M. Hariharan, Problem Solving and Programming in C, Pearson, 2025
source_files: examprep for srm ktr/syllabus.pdf (official, Regulations 2026, course page 62)
examprep for srm ktr/pps/pyqs and questions and theory/ (past papers and question banks, carrying the earlier course code)
courses.notes: The course code changed between regulations: the syllabus the learner supplied is Regulations 2026 and uses 26CSE1002J, while the past papers carry 21CSS101J from the earlier regulation. Both are recorded. The unit titles below are descriptive labels derived from the official session-by-session content; the official syllabus names the units only as 'Unit 1' to 'Unit 5' and does not give them titles. The unit numbering on the older papers does not map one-to-one onto the 2026 units, so a question's unit is recorded as the paper stated it and is not translated. The end-semester question-paper pattern is not in the syllabus: the only pattern available is the Cycle Test header on the CT papers - 25 marks, 50 minutes, Part A 10 x 1 - which is a cycle test, not the end-semester paper.

topics.title: Fundamentals of C: types, expressions and decision-making
Problem decomposition, functions and modular design
Nested loops, sorting, searching and memory use
Structures, dynamic memory and file handling
